items.stem: The basic event in reproduction is the creation of a:
items.answer: DNA copy
items.markingKey: (c) DNA copy.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Variation helps in the survival of a species.
Reason (R): Some variants may be able to live in changed environments.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Why do offspring from asexual reproduction show very little variation?
items.answer: Only one parent is involved and DNA is copied with only small errors.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: A population of bacteria in a pond includes some that can survive at 40 °C. If the pond heats up in summer, what will happen to the population, and why?
items.answer: Most bacteria die, but the heat-resistant variants survive and reproduce, so the population that remains is mainly heat-resistant.
items.markingKey: 1 mark most die. 1 mark variants survive. 1 mark population changes.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Offspring produced asexually are similar but not exactly identical to the parent.
Reason (R): DNA copying involves small inaccuracies.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Why is sexual reproduction considered to promote diversity of characters in the offspring, while asexual reproduction does not?
items.answer: Sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents through gametes (each with half the DNA), producing new combinations; asexual involves one parent with DNA copied nearly exactly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark two parents. 1 mark half DNA. 1 mark asexual.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The making of two copies of DNA in a cell before it divides."
items.answer: DNA copying
items.markingKey: (b) DNA copying is the making of two copies of DNA in a cell before it divides.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A group of individuals of the same species living in an area."
items.answer: a population
items.markingKey: (d) A population is a group of individuals of the same species living in an area.

items.stem: Which of these does NOT reproduce by spores?
items.answer: Hydra
items.markingKey: (a) Hydra.

items.stem: Which of these organisms reproduces by multiple fission?
items.answer: Plasmodium
items.markingKey: (b) Plasmodium reproduces by multiple fission. The others: banana – vegetative propagation; Hydra – budding; Rhizopus – spore formation.

items.stem: How does Plasmodium reproduce?
items.answer: By multiple fission: the nucleus divides many times and the cell splits into many daughter cells at once.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Group these organisms by mode of reproduction, multiple fission or binary fission: bacteria, Plasmodium.
items.answer: Multiple fission: Plasmodium. Binary fission: bacteria.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Multiple fission: Plasmodium. Binary fission: bacteria.

items.stem: Group these organisms by mode of reproduction, fragmentation or regeneration: Spirogyra, Planaria.

items.stem: Which of these organisms does NOT reproduce by vegetative propagation?
items.answer: bacteria
items.markingKey: (b) Bacteria reproduces by binary fission, not vegetative propagation. Each of the others (banana, Bryophyllum, potato) reproduces by vegetative propagation.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Growing new plants from cells of a growing tip in an artificial medium."
items.answer: tissue culture
items.markingKey: (b) Tissue culture is growing new plants from cells of a growing tip in an artificial medium.

items.stem: A farmer in Maharashtra grows sugarcane and bananas from cuttings and suckers, not seeds. Give two advantages and one disadvantage of this practice.
items.answer: Advantages: identical plants with known good traits; quick growth; plants that do not form seeds can be grown. Disadvantage: no variation, so a disease can destroy the whole crop.
items.markingKey: 2 marks advantages. 1 mark disadvantage.

items.stem: Which of these organisms reproduces by budding?

items.markingKey: (d) Rose reproduces by vegetative propagation. The others: Rhizopus – spore formation; Amoeba – binary fission; Plasmodium – multiple fission.

items.stem:
Read: In a school lab, Fatima observed bread mould under a microscope. She saw thread-like hyphae with tiny blob-like structures on top. She also saw a slide of yeast with small outgrowths, and one of Amoeba dividing into two.
(i) Name the blob-like structures and what they contain. (ii) Name the mode of reproduction in yeast. (iii) What is the process in Amoeba? (iv) Why do the spores of bread mould not germinate on dry bread?
items.answer: (i) Sporangia containing spores. (ii) Budding. (iii) Binary fission. (iv) Spores need moisture (and warmth) to germinate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma of:

items.stem: How is the process of pollination different from fertilisation?
items.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma; fertilisation is the fusion of the male germ cell with the egg in the ovule.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of sexual reproduction in a flowering plant in the correct order: (1) the zygote divides to form the embryo; (2) the male germ cell fuses with the egg to form a zygote; (3) a pollen tube grows through the style; (4) pollen lands on the stigma; (5) the ovule develops a tough coat and becomes a seed; (6) the tube reaches the ovule.
items.markingKey: Correct order: pollen lands on the stigma → a pollen tube grows through the style → the tube reaches the ovule → the male germ cell fuses with the egg to form a zygote → the zygote divides to form the embryo → the ovule develops a tough coat and becomes a seed.

items.stem: Why do germ cells have half the number of chromosomes of body cells? What would happen if they did not?
items.answer: So that when two germ cells fuse, the zygote has the normal (full) number; otherwise the amount of DNA would double in each generation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark half. 1 mark restoration. 1 mark doubling.

items.stem: How does the embryo get nourishment inside the mother's body?
items.answer: Through the placenta: villi on the embryo's side take glucose and oxygen from the mother's blood; wastes pass the other way.
items.markingKey: 1 mark placenta. 1 mark exchange.

items.stem:
Read: In 2011 the child sex ratio in some districts of India fell to about 830 girls per 1000 boys. The government banned prenatal sex determination and started the "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" campaign.
(i) What is meant by female foeticide? (ii) Why is prenatal sex determination banned? (iii) Who determines the sex of the child, mother or father? (iv) Suggest one way to improve the sex ratio.
items.answer: (i) Killing of a female foetus before birth. (ii) To stop female foeticide and maintain a healthy sex ratio. (iii) The father (X or Y chromosome in the sperm). (iv) Awareness campaigns, education of girls, strict enforcement of the law.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: What are the different methods of contraception? Explain how each works. Why should prenatal sex determination not be done?
items.answer: Barrier (condoms, diaphragm) – stop sperm reaching the egg and protect from STIs; hormonal (pills) – change hormonal balance so eggs are not released; copper-T/loop – placed in the uterus; surgical – vasectomy (vas deferens blocked) or tubectomy (fallopian tube blocked). Prenatal sex determination leads to female foeticide and a falling sex ratio; it is banned by law.
items.markingKey: 4 marks methods; 1 mark sex determination.

items.markingKey: (d) Vasectomy (blocking the vas deferens) is a surgical method. The others: oral contraceptive pills – a chemical (hormonal) method; condom – a barrier method; diaphragm – a barrier method.

items.stem: Which of these organisms reproduces by regeneration?
items.answer: Planaria
items.markingKey: (a) Planaria reproduces by regeneration. The others: sugarcane – vegetative propagation; yeast – budding; banana – vegetative propagation.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of sexual reproduction in a flowering plant in the correct order: (1) the male germ cell fuses with the egg to form a zygote; (2) the zygote divides to form the embryo; (3) the tube reaches the ovule; (4) pollen lands on the stigma; (5) a pollen tube grows through the style.
items.markingKey: Correct order: pollen lands on the stigma → a pollen tube grows through the style → the tube reaches the ovule → the male germ cell fuses with the egg to form a zygote → the zygote divides to form the embryo.

items.stem: Which of these is a part of the female reproductive system?
items.answer: oviduct (fallopian tube)
items.markingKey: (a) Oviduct (fallopian tube) is a part of the female reproductive system. The others: prostate gland – a part of the male reproductive system; seminal vesicles – a part of the male reproductive system; scrotum – a part of the male reproductive system.

items.stem: Classify these as a part of the male reproductive system or a part of the female reproductive system: vas deferens, uterus, scrotum, testes, oviduct (fallopian tube).
items.answer: A part of the male reproductive system: scrotum, testes, vas deferens. A part of the female reproductive system: oviduct (fallopian tube), uterus.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A part of the male reproductive system: scrotum, testes, vas deferens. A part of the female reproductive system: oviduct (fallopian tube), uterus.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Planaria reproduces by budding.
Reason (R): Planaria can regenerate from small pieces.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (Planaria shows regeneration/fragmentation); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of sexual reproduction in a flowering plant in the correct order: (1) the tube reaches the ovule; (2) the zygote divides to form the embryo; (3) the male germ cell fuses with the egg to form a zygote; (4) a pollen tube grows through the style; (5) the ovule develops a tough coat and becomes a seed.
items.markingKey: Correct order: a pollen tube grows through the style → the tube reaches the ovule → the male germ cell fuses with the egg to form a zygote → the zygote divides to form the embryo → the ovule develops a tough coat and becomes a seed.

items.stem: Classify these as a part of the stamen or a part of the pistil (carpel): style, filament, stigma, anther, ovary.
items.answer: A part of the stamen: anther, filament. A part of the pistil (carpel): ovary, stigma, style.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A part of the stamen: anther, filament. A part of the pistil (carpel): ovary, stigma, style.

items.stem: Why is DNA copying essential in reproduction?
items.answer: It passes the body design and features from the parent to the offspring, so the new cell can function like the parent.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Classify these as a part of the male reproductive system or a part of the female reproductive system: vagina, cervix, prostate gland, ovary, testes.
items.answer: A part of the male reproductive system: prostate gland, testes. A part of the female reproductive system: cervix, ovary, vagina.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A part of the male reproductive system: prostate gland, testes. A part of the female reproductive system: cervix, ovary, vagina.

items.stem: Which of these organisms does NOT reproduce by binary fission?
items.answer: potato
items.markingKey: (a) Potato reproduces by vegetative propagation, not binary fission. Each of the others (Amoeba, bacteria, Leishmania) reproduces by binary fission.

items.stem: Which of these organisms reproduces by binary fission?
items.answer: bacteria
items.markingKey: (d) Bacteria reproduces by binary fission. The others: Plasmodium – multiple fission; Mucor – spore formation; yeast – budding.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The period of adolescence during which reproductive tissues mature."
items.answer: puberty
items.markingKey: (c) Puberty is the period of adolescence during which reproductive tissues mature.

items.stem: Group these organisms by mode of reproduction, binary fission or fragmentation: Spirogyra, Leishmania.
items.answer: Binary fission: Leishmania. Fragmentation: Spirogyra.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Binary fission: Leishmania. Fragmentation: Spirogyra.
